title: Numerical Properties and Scalability of s-Step Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Methods
problem: s-step PCG reduces synchronization but has poor numerical properties; basis choice affects stability
motivation: Scalability vs accuracy trade-off; need stable s-step methods without sacrificing parallel efficiency
method: The method extends s-step PCG—a fast linear equation solver that groups computation steps to reduce how often processors must synchronize—to work with any mathematical basis (the underlying set of foundation vectors used in calculations). By supporting flexible basis selection, different bases can be tuned to maintain numerical accuracy while retaining the speed benefit. The researchers comprehensively analyze different bases to identify which provide the best balance between synchronization reduction and numerical stability.
key_novelty: The key insight is that s-step PCG's numerical stability can be controlled through basis selection—enabling methods that are both fast (low synchronization) and numerically accurate.
contributions: Generalization of s-step PCG to arbitrary basis types
First comprehensive comparison of s-step PCG variants
Theoretical stability analysis across basis choices
